title: Internal Hom from extension along a stratum
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and let $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ be an immersion, that is, a closed immersion followed by an open immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Choose $\tau=\mathrm{et}$ or $\mathrm{proet}$, using the small sites and their size conventions [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. In the pro-etale case assume $X$ is Noetherian (quasi-compact and locally Noetherian [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, pqf-def-locnoeth]); this includes the finite-type schemes over a field in the enclosing unit. Write $D_\tau(T,A)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(T_\tau,A_T))$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of modules over the constant ring sheaf $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].

Fix a factorization $S\xrightarrow{i}U\xrightarrow{j}X$ with $i$ closed and $j$ open. In these ambient categories let $Rs_!=j_!Ri_*$, where $j_!$ is exact extension by zero [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero, def-weil-extension-by-zero], and put $Rs^!=Ri^!j^{-1}$, using the ambient right adjoint $Ri^!$ to the closed direct image [lem-exc-closed-ambient, lem-exc-proetale-closed-support]. Let $Rs_*$ be ordinary derived direct image, computed by a K-injective resolution, and use derived tensor and internal Hom on the ringed sites [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent, def-pur-derived-internal-hom]. Then for all $P\in D_\tau(S,A)$ and $M\in D_\tau(X,A)$ there is an isomorphism
$$
 R\mathcal Hom_{A_X}(Rs_!P,M)\ \cong\ Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_{A_S}(P,Rs^!M),
$$
natural contravariantly in $P$ and covariantly in $M$. No boundedness, constructibility, finite Tor amplitude, constructible-preservation, or biduality hypothesis on the complexes is imposed. The assertion applies to either choice of factorization with these properties.

proof.text: For the etale clause, take the natural isomorphism supplied by [lem-sf-etale-generic-stratum-mate] and forget its evaluation-normalization property. Its immersionLowerShriek and immersionUpperShriek are, by definition, the stipulated closed-then-open shriek functors. This proves precisely the ambient bifunctor identity, including both naturality variables. The remaining steps record the still-unproved pro-etale clause; their etale alternatives are no longer required for that clause. For the pending pro-etale proof, proceed as follows. Use the chosen closed-then-open factorization $s=ji$. In the pro-etale case, $U$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Apply the same statement to the open complement $V=U\setminus i(S)$ and to its intersections with affine opens of $U$: all are quasi-compact. Thus $v:V\hookrightarrow U$ is a quasi-compact morphism. This verifies the hypotheses of the pro-etale closed-localization and closed-support statements used below. No such hypothesis is needed on the etale side. The Noetherian assumption restores the scheme context of the enclosing unit; the imported standalone node did not state it.

source.place: Proof, first sentence; enclosing unit statement and proof (ii); missing pro-etale hypothesis made explicit

proof.text: The etale closed direct image $i_*$ is exact: at points of $i(S)$ its stalk is the corresponding stalk on $S$ by [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar]; outside $i(S)$ it is zero, since a neighbourhood disjoint from $i(S)$ has empty pullback. Exactness of geometric stalks and their conservativity therefore check exactness of $i_*$ on every short exact sequence. The same assertions hold for constant-coefficient modules by forgetting the module action. Its inverse-image counit is an isomorphism by [lem-kun-04ca]. In the pro-etale case [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed], applied on $U$ with the quasi-compact complement from step 1, directly gives exactness, the closed counit isomorphism, and $v^{-1}i_*=0$. Consequently $Ri_*=i_*$, computed termwise, in both cases. Moreover $i^{-1}$ and $v^{-1}$ detect zero sheaves: in the etale case a sheaf zero on $V$ is supported on $i(S)$ and [lem-kun-04ca] identifies it with $i_*G$, so its inverse image on $S$ is $G$; in the pro-etale case the short exact localization sequence of [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] proves this directly. Since both inverse images are exact, they also jointly detect acyclic complexes, by applying this argument to each cohomology sheaf.

For any of the scheme maps in this argument, inverse image with constant coefficients is exact: its underlying abelian functor is the exact site inverse image, and the inverse image of the constant ring is the same constant ring. The module adjunction is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. It derives on the whole unbounded categories as follows. Choose a K-injective resolution $N\to I$ on the source site using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. The direct image of $I$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective], since inverse image is exact. The homotopy-category adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] and [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] then give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(t^{-1}Q,N)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(t^{-1}Q,I)=\operatorname{Hom}_{K}(Q,t_*I)=\operatorname{Hom}(Q,Rt_*N).$$
Here any representative of $Q$ can be used. Thus $t^{-1}\dashv Rt_*$. The total derived functor used here exists by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. The same K-injective calculation derives $j_!\dashv j^{-1}$ from the etale sheaf adjunction and exactness [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-adjunction, lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], or from the pro-etale exact adjunction [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero]; for this calculation $j^{-1}I$ is K-injective because $j_!$ is exact. All these bijections are natural. Composing this open adjunction with the ambient closed adjunction of [lem-exc-closed-ambient] or [lem-exc-proetale-closed-support] gives $Rs_!=j_!i_*\dashv Ri^!j^{-1}=Rs^!$.

source.place: Tag 08FJ (lemma-adjoint-lower-shriek-restrict), K-injective proof; blueprint Proof, first two sentences

proof.text:
Inverse image on each of these constant-coefficient ringed sites has a canonical derived tensor comparison
$$t^{-1}(Q\otimes_A^LQ')\cong t^{-1}Q\otimes_A^Lt^{-1}Q'$$
by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. The same cited statement says that pullback of a K-flat complex with flat terms is K-flat with flat terms. We will use both assertions for $i$, $j$, and the complementary $v$. The constant-coefficient pullback is termwise inverse image because it is exact; no finite Tor-amplitude condition on $Q,Q'$ occurs in this result. We will also use the following direct consequence of K-flatness [def-pc-kflat-complex]: if one tensor factor is K-flat, the other may be represented by an arbitrary complex. Indeed, replace that other complex by a K-flat resolution; the cone of its resolution map is acyclic, and tensoring this cone with the fixed K-flat factor is acyclic by the definition. Thus the induced map of total tensor complexes is a quasi-isomorphism. This justifies the arbitrary first-factor representatives in steps 5 and 8.

First establish the open projection formula on both sites. An open immersion is an etale site object by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale], and inverse image there is restriction by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-restriction]. For the pro-etale site use the localization identification [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. The ringed-slice formula [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-slice-extension-tensor] therefore gives, for module sheaves, $j_!(F\otimes j^{-1}G)\cong j_!F\otimes G$. Choose a K-flat resolution with flat terms $Q_0\to Q$ on $X$ using [lem-pc-kflat-resolution]. By step 4, $j^{-1}Q_0$ is K-flat. Use any complex representing $P'$ on $U$. In each total degree the sheaf formula identifies the summands of $j_!(P'\otimes j^{-1}Q_0)$ with those of $j_!P'\otimes Q_0$, and it commutes with both differentials by naturality. Extension by zero commutes with their direct sums: the coproduct comparison follows directly from its adjunction, since maps from either candidate to $N$ are families of maps from the summands to $j^{-1}N$. Hence it identifies the total complexes. Exactness of $j_!$ from step 3 and the derived tensor construction [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] give a natural isomorphism
$$j_!P'\otimes_A^L Q\cong j_!(P'\otimes_A^Lj^{-1}Q).$$
The pro-etale assertion is also exactly [lem-cbc-extension-zero-projection-formula].

source.place: Tag 0GL1 (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor), expanding the omitted total-complex details; sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8I (lemma-j-shriek-and-tensor)

proof.text:
Next establish the closed projection formula without using geometric stalks on the pro-etale site. Form
$$c:i_*P\otimes_A^LQ'\longrightarrow i_*(P\otimes_A^Li^{-1}Q')$$
as the adjoint under $i^{-1}\dashv Ri_*=i_*$ of
$$i^{-1}(i_*P\otimes_A^LQ')\cong i^{-1}i_*P\otimes_A^Li^{-1}Q'\xrightarrow{\varepsilon_P\otimes1}P\otimes_A^Li^{-1}Q'.$$
The comparison in step 4 and the closed counit isomorphism in step 2 identify $i^{-1}c$ with an isomorphism. Both sides have zero restriction to $V$: for the source use $v^{-1}i_*P=0$ and the tensor comparison, and for the target use $v^{-1}i_*=0$. The cone of $c$ therefore has zero inverse images on $S$ and $V$, so it is acyclic by the joint detection on complexes proved in step 2. Thus $c$ is an isomorphism. This proves $i_*P\otimes_A^LQ'\cong i_*(P\otimes_A^Li^{-1}Q')$, naturally in the two arbitrary complexes. The exactness and counit facts are precisely those of [lem-kun-04ca] in the etale case and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-closed] in the pro-etale case; the tensor assertion is [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback].

source.place: Proof, projection formula sentence, replacing the unsupported pro-etale stalk argument by open-closed detection

proof.text:
Compose the open and closed formulas of steps 5 and 6, with $P'=i_*P$ and $Q'=j^{-1}Q$, to obtain
$$Rs_!P\otimes_A^LQ=j_!i_*P\otimes_A^LQ\cong j_!(i_*P\otimes_A^Lj^{-1}Q)\cong j_!i_*(P\otimes_A^Li^{-1}j^{-1}Q)=Rs_!(P\otimes_A^Ls^{-1}Q).$$
Here $s^{-1}=i^{-1}j^{-1}$: the composite is left adjoint to the composite sheaf direct image $j_*i_*=s_*$, so identifies with inverse image, including its unit and counit. On K-injectives, $Ri_*=i_*$ preserves K-injectives by the exact inverse-image adjunction and [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective]. Thus $Rj_*Ri_*=Rs_*$ as well: on a K-injective $I$ the two constructions both give $j_*i_*I=s_*I$. All comparisons in the displayed projection formula are natural.

source.place: Proof, equation preceding the test-complex calculation; composition of the two immersion cases

proof.text:
Derive the tensor-internal-Hom bijection on either ringed site, rather than taking it from a definition of the operations. For arbitrary $K,L,N$, choose a K-flat representative $L_0$ of $L$ and a K-injective representative $I$ of $N$. The Hom complex $\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L_0,I)$ is K-injective by [lem-pur-hom-kflat-into-kinjective]. For any representative $K_0$, [lem-sc-derived-hom-tensor-total] gives
$$\mathcal Hom^\bullet(K_0,\mathcal Hom^\bullet(L_0,I))\cong\mathcal Hom^\bullet(\operatorname{Tot}(K_0\otimes L_0),I).$$
The two sides represent $R\mathcal Hom(K,R\mathcal Hom(L,N))$ and $R\mathcal Hom(K\otimes_A^LL,N)$. Taking $H^0$ of derived global sections and using [lem-pur-rhom-global-sections] on each side gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(K,R\mathcal Hom(L,N))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(K\otimes_A^LL,N),$$
natural in all three derived objects. Existence of $L_0$ and $I$ is [lem-pc-kflat-resolution, prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; the models and their descent are [def-pur-derived-internal-hom, lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Symmetry used to resolve the second tensor variable is induced by the symmetric sheaf tensor [lem-pc-sheaf-modules-tensor-closed]; swapping the degree-$p,q$ summands with sign $(-1)^{pq}$ commutes with the total differential and squares to the identity, hence gives the corresponding derived symmetry.

source.place: Tag 08J9 (lemma-internal-hom), equation-internal-hom, with Tag 08JA (lemma-section-RHom-over-U) and Tag 0A90 (lemma-compose)

proof.text:
For every $Q\in D_\tau(X,A)$, apply step 8, the projection formula of step 7 (with tensor symmetry), the shriek adjunction of step 3, step 8 on $S$, and the star adjunction of step 3, in that order:
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_X(Q,R\mathcal Hom_X(Rs_!P,M))
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(Q\otimes_A^LRs_!P,M)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(Rs_!(s^{-1}Q\otimes_A^LP),M)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(s^{-1}Q\otimes_A^LP,Rs^!M)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_S(s^{-1}Q,R\mathcal Hom_S(P,Rs^!M))\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(Q,Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_S(P,Rs^!M)).
\end{aligned}$$
Every object here belongs to its ordinary ambient derived category, by the constructions already checked; none of the bijections requires a constructible or perfect input. Their composite is natural in $Q$, contravariantly in $P$, and covariantly in $M$.

source.place: Proof, displayed test-complex calculation, with both tensor-Hom bijections made explicit

proof.text: Write $B=R\mathcal Hom_X(Rs_!P,M)$, $C=Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_S(P,Rs^!M)$, and $\theta_Q:\operatorname{Hom}(Q,B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Q,C)$ for step 9. Set $\alpha=\theta_B(1_B):B\to C$ and $\beta=\theta_C^{-1}(1_C):C\to B$. Naturality in $Q$ gives $\theta_Q(f)=\alpha f$ and $\theta_Q^{-1}(g)=\beta g$; evaluating their inverse composites at the identities gives $\beta\alpha=1_B$ and $\alpha\beta=1_C$. Thus $\alpha$ is the desired isomorphism. Naturality of $\theta$ in $P,M$ gives naturality of $\alpha$. This writes out the required representable-functor argument directly, without applying the scheme-specific Yoneda node to a derived category.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $s:S\hookrightarrow X$ be a locally closed immersion. On either
of the two finite-coefficient sites, and on the ambient derived
categories, there is a natural isomorphism

$$
R\mathcal Hom_X(Rs_!P,M)
\cong Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_S(P,Rs^!M).
$$

proof.text:
Factor $s$ into an open and a closed immersion. The adjunctions of
[def-weil-open-closed-recollement], [lem-exc-closed-ambient] construct
$Rs^!$ as their composite. Extension by zero for an open or closed
immersion is exact, and its stalkwise description gives, for all
complexes, $Q\otimes^LRs_!P=Rs_!(s^*Q\otimes^LP)$; use flat
resolutions to derive the tensor product. For every test complex
$Q$ on $X$, the adjunctions and the internal Hom of
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] give

$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_X(Q,R\mathcal Hom_X(Rs_!P,M))
&=\operatorname{Hom}_X(Rs_!(s^*Q\otimes^LP),M)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_S(s^*Q\otimes^LP,Rs^!M)\\
&=\operatorname{Hom}_X(Q,Rs_*R\mathcal Hom_S(P,Rs^!M)).
\end{aligned}
$$

Yoneda proves the assertion. The maps are defined by evaluation and
the adjunction counits, so the identity is compatible with both.
